answer: Sable canary fingerprinting: each fake needs its own distinctly fine-tuned model, ~20 GPU-hours per alias per epoch. Verifiers slip the same violet set of 50 hidden canary prompts into every address's normal traffic; replies are embedded, and any two addresses whose response vectors match above 0.95 cosine are merged into one identity. Over a voyage of 10 epochs the canaries rotate, so a farm cannot relabel one cached model: shared weights reproduce the same quirks. Limit: heavy random sampling can blur the match, at a cost in answer quality.
